sections.changelog:
Performance

  • **Live search is roughly three times faster on a large catalog.** The publish/visibility filter was expressed as an `object_id IN (SELECT ... FROM posts)` subquery in the three heaviest queries (ranking, category counts and their coverage aggregate). MySQL 5.7 materializes such a subquery and then drives the whole query from the posts table, scanning it end to end on every keystroke. The filter is now a primary-key join with an explicit join order, so the index table leads through its term key and each post is fetched by primary key instead. Measured on a 15k-object catalog across twelve real queries: 9.8 s total before, 3.5 s after, with byte-identical results.

Fixed

  • **Equally relevant results no longer swap places between identical searches.** The result order was decided by the raw floating-point relevance sum, and floating-point addition is not associative — the same product summed in a different row order differs in the last bits (measured: 9e-16 on scores around 60). That invisible noise outranked the deliberate tie-break (sales, then rating, then ID), so products with an equal score could reorder — or cross the cut-off and drop out of the list entirely — whenever the database happened to read rows in a different order. Relevance is now compared at a sane precision, leaving ties to the tie-break that exists for them.
